findings: Deleted stale Cargo-as-CI wording instead of adding a parallel exception path.
Kept the enforcement surface policy-driven through specs/buck2-authority-policy.json.
Release optimization is treated as measured artifact evidence only, not merge authority.
PGO and allocator experiments require representative workload labels and Buck2 handoff plans.
The scanner failed when pasteable Cargo commands appeared in the standard; wording was changed to non-pasteable exception language and the scanner now passes.
Cargo install/test/check/clippy/nextest/bench remain forbidden active-lane patterns.
The standard now gives a release-experiment sequence and explicit anti-patterns.
Cargo.toml comments point readers to the policy and say the profile is not CI authority.
TOML parse/profile assertion, JSON parse, Buck2 authority scanner, Buck2 policy target build, and diff hygiene passed.
Rejected keeping strip=symbols as the default because rustc warns symbol stripping can harm backtraces/profiling on some platforms.
Rejected documenting pasteable Cargo commands in the standard because the scanner and policy should prevent copy/paste CI regressions.
No secrets or tenant data touched.
The standard explicitly says strip is not a security/obfuscation control.
No performance readiness claim is made.
Profile, PGO, target-cpu, and allocator settings are classified as measurement candidates requiring service evidence.
Cargo release profile now defaults to strip=debuginfo, preserving symbol-table support relative to strip=symbols.
Symbols stripping remains an experiment only with incident-debug evidence.
Evidence names all validations and official sources.
Crash-reporting/profiling retention is now a required marker when strip/panic settings change.
Supports AC-0.16 automation ratchet by mapping the exception to a generated policy and Buck2 target.
Supports AC-0.17 by avoiding performance/production-readiness claims without evidence.
